get.summary: Get a timeline of recorded video
get.description:
The purpose of this route is to make visualization of any recording, motion or umd event easier. It shouldn't be used for an accuracy measure for available recordings.

The `storage` parameter in the request body is for consumers who'd like to know the storage source of the recording. There are different layers of storage, represented as `LAYER_X`, where `X` is an integer representing how immediate the layer is in terms of accessibility. As X value gets bigger, the layer that is accessed is likely to have higher latency. If the layer infromation is not important but you'd like to query all the available recordings, specify this parameter to the `ALL` value. The response to this request will contain all the recordings discovered, without the layer information. If the layer information is important, then you need to make separate queries for each layer, specifying the layer in the `storage` parameter.

In the response body, the `unloaded` parameter indicates a time range that has recorded video, motion events, or UMD events for a given camera. Use the `GET /media` route to get recorded video from this time range.

parameters.description: The session parameter returned by the login request
parameters.name: x-avg-session

parameters.description: The session parameter returned by the login request
parameters.name: session

parameters.description: The IDs of multiple cameras. **Note**: You can only use this field if the `id` field is empty.
parameters.name: cameraIds

parameters.description:
The requested interval length for the timeline in seconds.
    For example, if the scope is 1000_SECONDS, the returned intervals will have a length of at least
    1000 seconds if there is recorded video for the given camera
parameters.name: scope

parameters.description:
Must be a valid ISO 8601 string. Ex: yyyy-mm-ddThh:mm:ss.ffffff.
    This value should be a time earlier than the 'end' parameter. DEFAULT: 1 week before current date
parameters.name: start

parameters.description:
The minimum duration of UMD activity in milliseconds.
    DEFAULT: 0, so all the activity found in the start/end range will be returned
parameters.name: umdRange

parameters.description:
Specify the minimum amount of rareness of
  the UMD activity as a percentage. DEFAULT: 0, so all umd events will be returned
parameters.name: rareness

parameters.description:
Must be a valid ISO 8601 string. Ex: yyyy-mm-ddThh:mm:ss.ffffff.
    This value should be a time later than the 'start' parameter. DEFAULT: current time
parameters.name: end

parameters.description: The storage layer to get the timeline from. DEFAULT: `LAYER_1`
parameters.name: storage

put.summary: Update the video retention settings
put.description:
**Warning**: Updating these settings can result in data loss.

This call updates the retention settings for cameras connected to a server. The request only applies to the `cameraIds` entered.

Specify the maximum amount of time to keep recorded video on the server using the `maxRetention` parameter. Video older than this setting is deleted from the server, unless it is part of a protected bookmark. If the server runs out of space before this time, the oldest unprotected video will be deleted first.

To increase storage capacity, the ACC system can delete a portion of the higher resolution streams using the `streamRetentionAmount` parameter.

To use this parameter, the camera must have a secondary stream enabled.

The `streamRetentionAmount` parameter is an array with two values, [x, y].

- For JPEG cameras with 3 streams, specify the percent of video kept at full frame rate (x) and half frame rate (x + y). The ACC system keeps 100% of the quarter frame rate until it exceeds the `maxRetention` parameter.

- For H.264 and H.265 cameras with 2 streams, specify the percent of video kept at high resolution (x + y). Both x and y values are required in case the camera format changes to JPEG format. The ACC system keeps 100% of the low resolution stream until it exceeds the `maxRetention` parameter.

- For example, [0.6, 0.2] would indicate 60% full frame rate, 80% half frame rate and 100% quarter frame rate for JPEG cameras , while for H.264 cameras this would indicate 80% high resolution and 100% low resolution.

put.summary: Trigger a continuous or field of view PTZ action
put.description:
There are two modes of triggering a PTZ action: `continuous` and `fieldOfView`. Only one mode can be specified at a time.

**Continuous PTZ**

Used for triggering a continous PTZ action with a joystick or mouse-drag action, or zooming in or out.

You can call multiple `START` commands with varying values for `panAmount`, `tiltAmount` and `zoomAmount`.

- The last call will continue until another `START` or `STOP` command is received.

- Specify a `STOP` command when the mouse button or joystick is released.

- If there is no `STOP` command, the last call will continue until the end of the camera range is reached.

This mode requires visual verification of the video stream. Use the camera webUI or a thick client to view the stream while calling a command.

**Field Of View PTZ**

Used for changing the camera field of view (FOV). There are two modes of changing the FOV: `ROI` and `point`. Only one mode can be specified at a time.

- `ROI` zooms into a sub-region of the current camera FOV.

- `point` centers the FOV on a specified point within the current camera FOV.

For both `ROI` and `point` values, any unit can be used as long as it is consistent. The API normalizes the units.
